text:
olivia: Quick sync — proposing a conservative ramp plan for the 'fast-path' model toggle. Goal: avoid oscillation and give ops time to react. Need consensus on ramp steps, hold windows, telemetry gates, and an immediate kill path.

aj: +1. Suggest ramps: 5% -> 10% -> 20% -> 50% with a hold after each step. default holds = 4h, but add a speed-bump at 10% (2h) for manual QA.

tina: Agree on conservative steps. Also propose a regional hold for EU (start at 0 for EU for 24h) because of recent infra differences.

sam: For SRE: require two telemetry gates: (1) p99 latency not increase > 20% vs baseline, (2) error rate not exceed 0.5% absolute. If either fails, auto-roll back to model_v1.

priya: Ops note — ensure the circuit-breaker kick is synchronous. We should have a kill switch that flips at traffic-router level and a fallback mapping to the previous variant. Also capture active requests to let them drain for < 30s.

olivia: Good. Let's capture this in a flag config snippet so devs and infra know the contract. Draft config (for feature-flag system):

```
flag: fast_path_v2
default: disabled
ramp_steps: [5,10,20,50]
holds_hours: [4,2,4,24]
regional_overrides: {eu: 0}
telemetry_gates:
  - name: p99_latency
    threshold: 1.20  # allowed multiplier
  - name: error_rate
    threshold: 0.005 # absolute
kill_switch: true
fallback: model_v1
drain_seconds: 30
```

aj: Couple of implementation notes: ensure the router honors holds (no auto-advance unless explicit); add a short not-before timestamp for each step so we can script canned rollbacks.

tina: +1. Also let's add a shadow sampling during the 5% step to capture outputs for eval without affecting end users (shadow_rate: 20% of 5% traffic).

sam: I'll wire up the alerting: create two pager alerts (p99-latency-breach, error-rate-breach) with runbooks. If page fires, on-call should evaluate within 15 minutes and hit the kill switch if needed.

priya: Ops will prep the kill-switch runbook and test the path in staging tomorrow. Can we schedule a 30-min blackout window for emergency rollbacks during the first day?

olivia: Good call. Proposed timeline: start ramp tomorrow 09:00 PST to 5% in canary region (NA-only), hold 4h, then 10% speed-bump 2h, evaluate. EU remains at 0 for 24h. Document and links: https://redwood-internal/roadmaps/fast-path-v2 (please comment).

devops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/fast-path-v2 -> 2025-06-17T09:00:00Z (dry-run ready) :white_check_mark:

aj: One last ask: add a 'graceful-fallback' test in the CI that simulates router kill-switch and verifies no dropped requests beyond drain_seconds.

olivia: Noted — I'll add to the rollout checklist. If nobody objects, we finalize this plan by EOD and start prepping docs + runbooks. :shipit:
